title: Mathematics on arXiv — latest batch, Friday 9 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This batch is only two days old at the snapshot and independent attention/citation evidence is too sparse to rank by popularity. The ordering is an inferred, result-led selection, not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
sections.abstract: Studies whether the origin of rational homogeneous polynomial ODEs is globally asymptotically stable and reduces this decision problem across odd degrees to the cubic case.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that deciding global asymptotic stability is many-one complete for every odd degree at least three in every sufficiently large dimension, and in particular is undecidable for cubic vector fields in a fixed dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients; the fixed-dimension cubic conclusion is for a dimension whose existence is established by the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The reduction is highly indirect and technical; the abstract does not give an explicit smallest dimension for cubic undecidability.

sections.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
sections.abstract: Derives worst-case noisy-regression sample thresholds for known subspaces of low-degree Boolean-cube functions by quantifying how their energy can concentrate on rarely sampled inputs.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed q₀<1/2 and degree 1≤k≤q₀d, the worst-subspace sample threshold for the stated minimax parametric error is (m+t) exp(E_{d,k}+O(k^{1/3})); the authors also show that noisy estimation can cost exponentially more samples than noiseless identification.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Gaussian regression with squared population L₂ loss, uniform random inputs on the d-dimensional Boolean cube, a known m-dimensional subspace of degree-at-most-k functions, and the confidence and fixed-constant conditions stated in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The matching lower bound is established under the additional condition m≤binom(d,⌊k^{1/3}⌋) or t≥m; it is not claimed there for every feasible subspace dimension and confidence regime.

sections.title: A Complete Proof of Mueller--Ho Conjecture
sections.abstract: Classifies the minimizing lattice shapes and relative shifts for a two-component Bose-gas energy built from a theta function and a shifted theta function as the interaction parameter varies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that minimizers, up to modular equivalence, pass through specified triangular, intermediate, square, and rectangular lattice configurations with relative shifts across three interaction thresholds, thereby claiming to prove the Mueller–Ho conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Minimize θ(1;z)+αJ(z;a,b) over z in the upper half-plane and shifts (a,b)∈R², for α∈[0,1]; the variables model lattice shape and relative displacement in a two-component Bose gas.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract states that three ordered thresholds exist but does not provide their explicit values; the classification is for this particular theta-energy model and is an author-claimed preprint result.

sections.title: A counterexample to the Erdős--Sós bipartite-link conjecture
sections.abstract: Constructs 3-uniform hypergraphs whose link graphs are all bipartite yet whose edge density asymptotically exceeds the conjectured one-quarter threshold.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims examples with edge density at least 0.250000356 > 1/4 for all sufficiently large n, disproving the stated (1/4+o(1)) binom(n,3) upper-bound conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraphs subject to every link graph being bipartite; the construction is asserted for all sufficiently large n.
sections.unique_caveat: The improvement over 1/4 is numerically small, and the abstract does not specify the finite size at which the construction applies; the asymptotic counterexample does not by itself determine the optimal density.

sections.title: Strong RSW estimates for the FK-Ising model on s-embeddings
sections.abstract: Establishes strong Russo–Seymour–Welsh crossing estimates for the FK-Ising model on s-embeddings under a uniformly bounded geometry condition.
sections.claimed_result: Under the stated geometry condition, the authors prove crossings of rough topological quadrilaterals even with unfavorable boundary conditions, then obtain standard consequences including quasi-multiplicativity of arm events and fractal cluster properties.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: FK-Ising on s-embeddings whose relevant tangential quadrilaterals have uniformly comparable edge lengths and angles bounded below; near-critical regular-grid applications below the correlation-length scale are discussed.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem depends on the uniformly bounded geometry hypothesis; the abstract does not assert the same strong estimates for arbitrary highly irregular embeddings.

sections.title: The sharp $L^2$-Michael--Simon inequality
sections.abstract: Proves a sharp Sobolev-type inequality coupling the gradient and mean curvature of an immersed manifold, and characterizes equality cases.
sections.claimed_result: For n≥3 and an isometric immersion into Euclidean space, the authors prove the stated sharp L² Michael–Simon inequality for all u∈W^{1,2}(Σ) and derive related mean-curvature/volume inequalities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: An n-dimensional Riemannian manifold isometrically immersed in Euclidean space; the inequality includes the mean-curvature potential and critical Sobolev exponent 2n/(n−2).
sections.unique_caveat: The stated inequality is for dimensions n≥3 and the specified isometric-immersion setting; equality and extensions beyond the stated conformal ambient settings need the paper's precise hypotheses.

sections.title: Lower bounds for Ramsey numbers: $\mathrm{R}(6,8)\ge 135$ and $\mathrm{R}(8,10)\ge 345$
sections.abstract: Gives explicit two-colourings establishing improved lower bounds for two Ramsey numbers, checked by two independently written exhaustive clique-verification programs.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves R(6,8)≥135 and R(8,10)≥345, improving the cited April 2026 survey bounds of 134 and 343 using colorings of K134 and K344 without the prohibited monochromatic cliques.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-colour Ramsey numbers avoiding a red K6 / blue K8, and a red K8 / blue K10; the proof rests on explicit coloring witnesses and exhaustive checks.
sections.unique_caveat: The new bounds establish lower bounds only, not exact Ramsey numbers; witnesses found with local search need certificates/checking code to be reproducible for independent computational auditing.
